name: AutoML-Zero: Evolving Machine Learning Algorithms From Scratch
family: evolutionary program search for learning algorithms

sources.title: AutoML-Zero: Evolving Machine Learning Algorithms From Scratch

principle: Represents candidate ML algorithms as short programs assembled from basic mathematical operations, with Setup, Predict, and Learn functions, and searches the program space using regularized evolution. Candidate quality is measured on task performance; the paper demonstrates rediscovery of backpropagation-based networks and other learned procedures.
learning_rule: Search procedure: initialize a population; repeatedly select a candidate by tournament, mutate its program, evaluate on task training/validation examples, and replace population members. Each candidate's Learn function updates its model state; no single fixed update equation characterizes all discovered candidates.
learning_signals: Task training examples and validation loss/accuracy used to evaluate candidates
Evolutionary selection based on candidate task performance
backprop_notes: The outer search is regularized evolution, not gradient backpropagation through candidate programs. However, discovered algorithms can use backpropagation: the paper explicitly reports rediscovering a two-layer neural network trained with gradient descent/backpropagation; other reported candidates use distinct update mechanisms. Thus the method cannot be characterized as uniformly no-backprop.
limitations: Not evaluated on Crafter in the inspected paper text.
Search is task- and representation-dependent; the framework optimizes performance on the provided supervised tasks rather than discovering a general reward-free agent.
An evolutionary outer loop avoids gradient backprop through the search, but candidate algorithms may themselves use backpropagation.
notes: Opened arXiv abstract and HTML full text (Sections 3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.2; Figures 1–5; Supplementary Tables S1 and section S3) and the Google Research repository page. `uses_extrinsic_reward=no` means no RL reward signal is reported for this supervised-task algorithm search; task labels/validation metrics do drive selection. Crafter values are omitted because none were found.

name: VeLO: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers by Scaling Up

sources.title: VeLO: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers by Scaling Up

principle: VeLO is a learned optimizer trained across a distribution of optimization tasks. At inner-loop use it consumes gradient and parameter/loss statistics to produce parameter updates; meta-training uses Evolution Strategies (ES) rather than differentiating through the complete inner optimization trajectory.
learning_rule: Inner loop: θₜ₊₁ = θₜ + VeLO(∇L(θₜ), parameter/loss statistics, progress). Meta-loop: evaluate optimizer parameters on full inner runs and use an ES estimate of the meta-objective gradient to update the optimizer; the paper optimizes final inner-run training loss. Exact architecture and training details are in Sections 3.1–3.3.
learning_signals: Task-loss gradients and parameter/loss statistics are inputs to the learned optimizer
Final training loss after inner optimization is the meta-objective
backprop_notes: The inner optimizer relies on task gradients, so its application involves gradient-based parameter optimization (the paper describes gradients as inputs). The outer meta-optimization uses Evolution Strategies rather than backpropagation through the inner trajectory. Thus it does not satisfy a strict no-gradient/no-backprop criterion for the learner as a whole.
limitations: The paper's RL evaluation is not a Crafter result; Crafter was not found in the inspected text.
VeLO is a learned optimizer, not an independently reward-free RL algorithm; task losses and gradients remain required.
The paper reports very large meta-training compute requirements (approximately 4,000 TPU-months).
notes: Opened arXiv abstract and HTML full text (Sections 2–3; Section 4.4.4; code link in the paper). `uses_extrinsic_reward=no` denotes the loss-based optimizer-training objective, not evidence that VeLO provides an autonomous reward-free RL agent. No Crafter result included. WebFetch pagination prevented reliable verification of detailed RL results; those are therefore not encoded.
